context_requirements: Intact autophagy machinery (ATG genes, BECN1, PIK3C3) for autophagic flux
Functional lysosomal degradation for late-stage autophagy
mTORC1 activity or upstream PI3K/AKT signaling to be inhibited for canonical induction
For mTOR-independent inducers (e.g., trehalose), AMPK activation or p38 MAPK/Foxo1 signaling
Stress-responsive transcription factors (FOXO, ATF4, CHOP) for transcriptional feedback
falsifiers: No increase in autophagy-related landmark transcripts (e.g., SQSTM1, BNIP3, BECN1) at 6 or 24 h in any responsive line
No decrease in mTOR pathway or proliferation-related landmark transcripts at 24 h
Uniform absence of transcriptional response across all nine cell lines
Predominant upregulation of proliferation genes rather than downregulation

evidence.supports: Isoliquiritigenin, a natural autophagy inducer, induces autophagy and cell cycle arrest in MCF-7/ADR breast cancer cells
MIR155 induces autophagy by targeting MTOR pathway components RHEB, RICTOR, and RPS6KB2, and attenuates proliferation with G1/S arrest
Trehalose, an mTOR-independent autophagy inducer, activates autophagy via p38 MAPK and Foxo1 in insulin-resistant myocardium
Arsenic trioxide acts as an autophagy inducer in glioblastoma cells, with autophagy inhibition modulating cytotoxicity
Trehalose induces autophagy in human podocytes via an mTOR-independent, AMPK-associated mechanism
